title: ABG methodology: equipment, prerequisites and procedure
guide: Equipment (ABG analyzer, 1 ml heparinized syringe with 0.5 ml heparin and no excess, 70% alcohol wipe and gauze, gloves and cover roll) and prerequisites (> 50% blood, syringe 3 ml or less, no air bubbles because they cause ↑PO₂/↓PCO₂, cold chain maintained). Allen's test determines radial artery patency; the wrist of the non-dominant hand is extended 20–30°, the radial artery palpated, the area sterilised and the needle inserted at 45°, then capped and transported.

title: Precautions, the delay table, contraindications and sites
guide: Precautions: flush with 0.5 ml 1 : 1000 heparin and empty the syringe (excess heparin → dilutional ↓HCO₃⁻ and ↓PCO₂), transport earliest via cold chain; delay changes pH 0.01, pCO₂ 1 mmHg and pO₂ 0.1% per 10 minutes at 37°C, versus 0.001, 0.1 mmHg and 0.01% iced at 4°C. Contraindications: abnormal Allen's test, local infection or distorted anatomy, severe peripheral vascular disease, active Raynaud's syndrome. Sites: radial, femoral, brachial, axillary, dorsalis pedis. Measured parameters (pH, pCO₂, pO₂, cCa²⁺, cCl⁻, cK⁺, cNa⁺, cGlucose, hematocrit) yield the derived ones (HCO₃⁻, anion gap, base excess).

title: The primary problems, reading methods and the Boston method
guide: Four primary problems: metabolic acidosis, metabolic alkalosis, respiratory acidosis (↑PaCO₂) and respiratory alkalosis (↓PaCO₂), the respiratory arms being further labelled acute or chronic. Three reading methods: Boston, Copenhagen, Stewarts. Boston normal values: pH 7.4, pCO₂ 40 mmHg, HCO₃⁻ 24 mEq/L, with [H⁺] = 24 × PaCO₂/HCO₃⁻ and [HCO₃⁻] = 24 × PaCO₂/H⁺; a valid ABG requires the calculated [HCO₃⁻] to lie within ±2 mEq of the venous sample. Step 1: pH < 7.4 acidosis, > 7.4 alkalosis.

title: Steps 2 and 3: primary abnormality and compensation
guide: Step 2: HCO₃⁻ and PaCO₂ following the line of pH identifies the primary problem — decreased pH with ↓HCO₃⁻ = metabolic acidosis or with ↑PaCO₂ = respiratory acidosis; increased pH with ↑HCO₃⁻ = metabolic alkalosis or with ↓PaCO₂ = respiratory alkalosis. Step 3 compensation: metabolic acidosis ↓HCO₃⁻/↓PaCO₂ (respiratory alkalosis) and metabolic alkalosis ↑HCO₃⁻/↑PaCO₂ (respiratory acidosis), with ↓1 mEq/L HCO₃⁻ → ↓1.2 mmHg pCO₂ and ↑1 mEq/L → ↑0.7 mmHg pCO₂; respiratory acidosis ↑PaCO₂/↑HCO₃⁻ (metabolic alkalosis) and respiratory alkalosis ↓PaCO₂/↓HCO₃⁻ (metabolic acidosis), with ↑10 mmHg pCO₂ → ↑1 mEq/L (acute) or ↑4 mEq/L (chronic) HCO₃⁻ and ↓10 mmHg pCO₂ → ↓2 mEq/L (acute) or ↓4 mEq/L (chronic).

title: Adequacy of compensation and the compensatory limits
guide: Adequacy flowchart: for metabolic acidosis/respiratory alkalosis a compensatory metabolite ≤ expected value means adequate compensation and between expected and normal means partial compensation; for metabolic alkalosis/respiratory acidosis the rule is mirrored (≥ expected value = adequate). Compensatory limits: respiratory acidosis ↑up to 30 mEq/L HCO₃⁻ (acute) and ↑up to 45 mEq/L (chronic); respiratory alkalosis ↓up to 20 mEq/L (acute) and ↓up to 12–14 mEq/L (chronic).

title: Anion gap, osmolal gap and delta ratio
guide: Anion gap: measured cation + unmeasured cation = measured anion + unmeasured anion, so mc − ma = ua − uc and AG = uc − ua = Na⁺ − (HCO₃⁻ + Cl⁻) = 12 ± 2 mEq/L, with corrected AGc = AG + 2.5 (4.5 − S.albumin). Osmolal gap = measured osmolality (osmomoter) − calculated osmolality, where calculated osmolality = 2(Na) + BUN/2.8 + Glucose/18 + 1.25 × EtOH; normal < 10 mOsm/kg and ≥ 10 mOsm/kg suggests unmeasured osmotically active molecules such as methanol or ethylene glycol. Delta ratio = ΔAG/ΔHCO₃⁻, where ΔAG = measured AG − normal AG: < 1 = HAGMA + NAGMA, 1–2 = HAGMA, > 2 = HAGMA + metabolic alkalosis.
